lemma: CONDITIONAL EXTRACTION LEMMA (candidate, not yet checked against TR25-045). Let T be a bounded-arithmetic theory and let T prove a Pi^b_2-type statement forall x exists y forall z A(x,y,z) (A sharply bounded). KPT witnessing gives a Student-Teacher game in which the Student is the class of functions that T's witnessing theorem provides: for T = PV_1 this class is polynomial time with polynomially many rounds. Hence a PV_1 proof of a lower bound yields a P-Student, not a uniform AC0[qpoly] Student. Carmosino-Grosser's P != NP implication (as stated in the search snippet) takes a uniform AC0[qpoly] Student that generates truth tables of super fixed-polynomial circuit complexity. The P-Student class is larger, so the premise of the implication is not supplied by the PV_1 extraction alone. The link holds only for a theory whose witnessing class is uniform AC0[qpoly].

lemma: DEPTH-2 SIZE LEMMA (repair of the refuted depth-2 test). For every f on n>=1 variables: f has a DNF with |f^-1(1)| terms and a CNF with |f^-1(0)| clauses, so min(DNF terms, CNF clauses) <= 2^(n-1). Tight for parity_n: any term with k<n literals is satisfied by points of both parities, so it is not an implicant; every DNF for parity_n uses only full minterms and needs 2^(n-1) terms (dually for CNF). Consequence: the naive depth-2 size measure (terms or clauses) cannot exceed 2^(n-1), so a separation in K12-D2 needs a different measure (wires, fan-in, or a restricted class). This closes no obligation and is not P vs NP progress.
